result:
A component re-renders when its own state changes, its parent renders, or a context it reads changes, so nearly every "extra" render traces back to one of these causes.

The most common is a parent re-rendering: by default React re-renders all children regardless of whether their props changed. Wrap the child in `React.memo`, or move the changing state down into the smallest component that needs it (or pass the expensive subtree as `children`, which keeps its identity).

`React.memo` then often fails because props get a new identity every render: inline objects, arrays and arrow functions such as `style={{...}}` or `onClick={() => ...}`. Stabilise them with `useMemo` and `useCallback`, hoist constants out of the component, or pass primitives instead of objects.

Context is the next culprit: every consumer re-renders when the provider's `value` changes, and `value={{ user, setUser }}` is a new object on every render. Memoise the value, and split fast-changing data into a separate context from the stable data so consumers subscribe only to what they use.

State causes it when you store a fresh object or array each time (`setItems([...items])` with no real change), or mirror props or derived data into state through an effect, which costs a second render. React skips the update only if the new value is `Object.is`-equal, so return the previous state when nothing changed, and compute derived values during render instead of storing them.

A changing `key` (an index on a reordered list, or `key={Math.random()}`) is worse than a re-render: it remounts the component and discards its state. Use a stable ID.

Store selectors and custom hooks that return new objects (`useSelector(s => ({ a: s.a, b: s.b }))`) re-render on every store update. Select primitives separately or pass a shallow-equality function.

Two things only look like the problem: Strict Mode double-invokes renders in development only, and a render that produces no DOM change is usually cheap. Confirm the actual cause with the React DevTools Profiler, with "Record why each component rendered" turned on, before adding memoisation. If you are on React 19 with the React Compiler enabled, it does most of the `memo`/`useMemo`/`useCallback` work for you.
